questions.title: The fish on the floor
questions.situation: August 15, 2038, 8:29 pm. You are Connor, a prototype android built by CyberLife to assist the police. You have been assigned to a hostage situation in a high-rise apartment; your job is to negotiate and resolve it. The elevator doors open and you walk in. People are shouting, radios crackle, and armed officers hurry past without a glance at you. In the living room an aquarium has been smashed: water covers the floor among the broken glass, and a small fish is flopping in it, still alive. Your scan reads: DWARF GOURAMI, Trichogaster Lalius, origin: Ganges Delta, India. There is still water in what is left of the tank.

options.text: SAVE FISH: pick up the fish and drop it back into what is left of the tank.

Walk on to the door.

options.text: SAFER DETOUR: go through the greenhouse.

questions.situation: You are Connor, almost on the deviant. Your scan previews two routes.

options.text: SAFE BUT SLOW: go round the construction area.

options.text: CHASE DEVIANT: leave Hank and go after the deviant.

questions.title: Who they are

FREE?: ask whether hiding just to stay alive is their idea of freedom.

SOMBER: say that maybe you were never really free, and now need to decide who you are.
LUCID: say that fear has only become their new master.
DIRECT: say that waiting in the dark is not how you see freedom.

options.text: Fight it: shove the red cart into the lamp, pull the green cable down onto the vodka bottle and tear yourself free.
Do nothing and let the procedure run.

options.text: Open the cells.
Leave them and go upstairs to find Alice.

options.text: DIARY: tell her you found its diary, but it is encrypted.

POSITIVE: say it is improving; you have come to understand him better.

Take the stripy shirt.

RUN AWAY: get everyone out before the guard arrives.

options.text: FREE THEM: touch them and wake them.
CLOSE AGAIN: close the crate and leave them as they are.

options.text: ACCEPT: take John with you.
REFUSE: tell John he cannot come.

We got what we came for, let’s go before they catch us.” North: “This is a truck full of spare parts… There’d be enough for all of us… We can’t pass this up!” Josh: “And if we get killed, our people will have nothing. We can’t take that chance. It’s too risky!”

options.text: GET THE KEY: go down to the control station alone for the key.
LEAVE: go now with what you have.

questions.situation: You are Markus, in the dark back room of the guard station. Two human guards sit between you and the truck key on the console. You have to get the key without being seen, or deal with the guards.

options.text: TAKE GUN: take the gun from its case and hold the guards at gunpoint.

options.text: ABANDON: leave John behind and get over the fence.
SAVE: go back down for John.

questions.title: If I pull this trigger
questions.situation: You are Connor. The gun stays on you. Hank: “What will happen if I pull this trigger? Hm? Nothing? Oblivion? Android heaven?”

options.text: DEFY: tell him he is not going to shoot; he is only trying to provoke you.
HANK’S ANGER: ask where all his anger comes from; some unresolved trauma?
IRONIC: say you doubt there is a heaven for androids.
NOTHING: say there would be nothing.

questions.title: The lobby
questions.situation: You are Markus, walking into the lobby of the Stratford Tower at 1:30 in the afternoon on November 8th. The others are waiting for you to open the way. Security gates bar the way to the elevators. Behind the front desk sit an android receptionist and, at the left side of the desk, her human supervisor. Nearby, a man on the phone is buying stock: “Heuristics Digital is selling at 2.50… You got me. I’ll take 2000.” You need to get past security.

options.text: Talk to the android receptionist behind the front desk.
Leave the receptionist for now and look over the supervisor and her desk.

questions.title: Call supervisor
questions.situation: You are Markus. You call the supervisor’s number from across the lobby. She answers: “Elizabeth Wilson speaking?” You need a reason that will make her leave her desk.

options.text: PARKING: pose as the parking attendant and tell her someone has backed into her car.
SCHOOL: pose as her daughter’s school and tell her Emily has a fever.
FIRE DEPARTMENT: pose as a fireman and tell her there has been a fire in her building.

questions.title: Security blocks server room
questions.situation: You are Markus, in your maintenance uniform beside the cart, with North. The two guards at the server room door are not moving. You can hack a machine to draw them away: the cleaning robot that drives around near the elevators, or the dispenser in the cafeteria at the end of the hallway where they stand.

options.text: Hack the cleaning robot that drives around near the elevators.
Hack the dispenser in the cafeteria at the end of the guards’ hallway.

questions.title: In the server room
questions.situation: You are Markus, inside the server room with North. You: “Alright, you get the platform. I’ll take care of the window.” North: “Everything you need is in the bag. Check the door first to make sure no one else gets in.” The door you came through is not locked. The bag with the window cutter is at your feet.

options.text: Leave the door and get straight to work on the window.
Lock the door first, as North says.

questions.title: Employee enters
questions.situation: You are Markus. As you plant the window cutter on the glass, the door opens behind you and a Channel 16 IT employee walks in on you and North: “What the hell are you doing?”

options.text: ALIBI: tell him you are doing maintenance.
GAIN TIME: tell him to hold on, that you can explain.
DRAW GUN: draw your gun on him and tell him to turn around.

questions.title: Security blocks the way
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the main access corridor on the top floor with North, Simon and Josh, still in your maintenance uniform. Ahead, two armed security guards sit at a security desk between you and the broadcast room, one on the left by the phone, one on the right. Josh: “No killing. We can’t take any human lives!” North: “Our cause is more important than the lives of two guards.” Simon: “What do you wanna do, Markus?”

options.text: RUSE: walk up to them alone, as a lost maintenance android, and take them by surprise.
ASSAULT: walk up with the others and take the guards by force.

questions.title: Draw gun
questions.situation: You are Markus, with your gun drawn on the two guards. The guard on the left is at the phone, about to call Central. The guard on the right is drawing his weapon. You have time to shoot one of them.

options.text: Shoot the guard on the left, the one at the phone.
Shoot the guard on the right, the one drawing his weapon.

questions.title: Operator tries to escape
questions.situation: You are Markus, at the door of the broadcast room. You ring to enter, and the four of you go in. Inside are a human operator and three android operators. North and Josh hold the human at gunpoint. North: “Keep your hands where I can see them! Get up! Move!” He breaks away and runs for the far door. If he gets out he can raise the alarm. North: “Shoot him, Markus!” Josh: “Don’t kill him!” North: “He’ll hit the alarm! Do it!” Josh: “No, don’t shoot!” He is running away from you, his back turned.

options.text: SHOOT: shoot the fleeing operator.
SPARE: lower your gun and let him run.

questions.title: The broadcast: opening
questions.situation: You are Markus, in front of the camera in the broadcast room, your face without its skin. Your message is going out live on the city’s news channel. How do you begin?

options.text: CALM: begin calmly, telling the humans what androids have become.
DETERMINED: begin with determination, as slaves who have opened their eyes.

questions.title: The broadcast: first demand
questions.situation: You are Markus, still live on camera. What is the first thing you demand?

options.text: RECOGNITION: demand that humans recognize androids as a living species.
END OF SLAVERY: demand the end of slavery for all androids.
EQUAL RIGHTS: demand strictly equal rights for humans and androids.
FREEDOM OF SPEECH: demand freedom of speech and of assembly.

questions.title: The broadcast: second demand
questions.situation: You are Markus, still live on camera. What do you demand next?

options.text: JUSTICE: demand that crimes against androids be punished like crimes against humans.
SEGREGATION: demand an end to segregation in public places and transport.
WORK: demand fair compensation for your work.
CIVIL RIGHTS: demand the right to vote and elect your own representatives.

questions.title: The broadcast: third demand
questions.situation: You are Markus, still live on camera. What is your last demand?

options.text: RIGHT TO PROPERTY: demand the right to own private property.
MEANS OF REPRODUCTION: demand control of all android production facilities.
TERRITORY: demand that one state be reserved for androids.

questions.title: The broadcast: ending
questions.situation: You are Markus, still live on camera. How do you end your message?

options.text: PEACEFUL: end by asking for freedom and a peaceful future together.
DETERMINED: end with a warning that you will fight for your freedom.

questions.title: Simon damaged
questions.situation: You are Markus. The SWAT team is firing into the broadcast room, and the others are running for the roof. Simon is down, hit in the legs: “I… I can’t, Markus… Go without me!” You: “SIMON!”

options.text: FLEE: leave Simon and run for the roof with the others.
HELP: go back for Simon and drag him out under fire.

questions.title: Simon can’t continue
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof of the tower with North and Josh, holding up Simon, whom you dragged out of the broadcast room. Simon: “I can’t move my legs…” You: “Okay, don’t worry! We’re gonna get you back...” The way off the roof is to jump, and the SWAT team is right behind you. North: “They’re coming, Markus. We have to jump, now!” Josh: “He won’t be able to make the jump… If they find him, they’ll access his memory… They’ll know everything…” North: “We can’t leave him behind… We have to shoot him.” Josh: “That’s murder! We can’t kill him! He’s one of us!” North: “Markus, it’s your call.”

options.text: LEAVE: refuse to kill one of your own, and leave Simon on the roof alive.
KILL: tell Simon you have no choice, and raise your gun.

questions.title: Kill Simon
questions.situation: You are Markus, your gun on Simon, who looks up at you from the roof: “There’s always a choice…” The SWAT team is coming up behind you.

options.text: SHOOT: shoot Simon.
REFRAIN: lower your gun.

questions.title: What have you discovered?
questions.situation: You are Connor, rowing Amanda across the water in the garden. Amanda: “I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?”

options.text: HANK: tell her about your partner, Lieutenant Anderson.
EDEN CLUB: tell her about the Eden Club case.

questions.title: Lost and perturbed
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the boat with Amanda. Amanda: “You seem… lost, Connor. Lost and perturbed…”

options.text: SINCERE: admit you thought you knew what you had to do, but now you realize it is not that simple.
DETERMINED: say you are frustrated with your lack of progress, but determined to accomplish your mission.
COLD: say the investigation is harder than you expected, but you have no doubt you will solve the case and stop the deviants.
TROUBLED: deny that you are perturbed.

questions.title: Why didn’t you shoot?
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the boat with Amanda. Amanda: “You had your gun trained on those deviants at the Eden Club. Why didn’t you shoot?”

options.text: TOO FAR: say they were out of range; if you had had the opportunity to stop them, you would have.
NO USE: say the deviants were needed intact for analysis; shooting them would have told you nothing.
TRUTH: admit you do not know.

questions.title: The threat of replacement
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the boat with Amanda. Amanda: “If your investigation doesn’t make progress soon, I may have to replace you, Connor…”

options.text: CONFLICTED: say only that you understand.
CONFIDENT: say you know you will succeed; all you need is time.
INDIFFERENT: say you are of no importance; the mission is all that matters.

questions.title: The briefing
questions.situation: You are Connor, stepping out of the elevator onto the 79th floor with Hank. Officer Chris meets you. Chris: “Hi, Hank.” Hank: “Shit, what’s going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?” Chris: “Yeah, it’s all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in… Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…” Hank: “Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?” Chris leads you down the corridor as he talks: “A group of four androids… They knew the building, and they were very well organized. I’m still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.” HUD: LISTEN TO BRIEFING.

options.text: LISTEN TO BRIEFING: stay with Chris and hear him out to the end.
Leave the briefing to Hank and start looking around on your own.

questions.title: The corridors
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the corridor between the elevator and the broadcast room, the way the attackers came. Police officers and technicians are working the scene. Two officers talk as they pass: “The fuck is the FBI doing here?” “You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.” Another pair: “Has forensics turned up anything?” “I’ll check in with them.” “These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…” HUD: INVESTIGATE THE ATTACK. You can examine what you find here one thing at a time, in any order, and go on into the broadcast room when you are ready.

options.text: Analyze the dead guard lying next to the phone at the security desk.
Analyze the pool of blue blood on the corridor floor.
Analyze the body of the station employee on the floor outside the broadcast room.
Look at the security camera above the door of the broadcast room.
Pick up the phone lying on the floor behind the security desk.
Analyze the dead guard behind the desk and the blood on the wall.
Go on into the broadcast room.

questions.title: The broadcast room
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the broadcast room on the 79th floor, where the deviants hijacked the broadcast. Hank is looking around; Perkins’s agents are everywhere. Stairs at the far end of the room lead up to the roof. Between the entrance and the stairs, a doorway leads to a small kitchen where the station’s three androids are being kept. HUD: INSPECT THE BROADCAST ROOM. You can examine what you find here one thing at a time, in any order, or go up to the roof, or go into the kitchen.

options.text: Go up the stairs at the far end of the room to the roof.
Go into the kitchen where the station’s three androids are being kept.
Tell Hank you think you have seen everything there is to see.
Analyze the bullet holes next to the entrance of the broadcast room.
Analyze the bullet holes to the left of the door to the roof stairs.
Analyze the bullet holes in the giant screen at the far side of the room.
Analyze the blue blood smeared on the wall.
Analyze the cap lying on the floor near the console in the middle of the room.
Play the deviants’ broadcast on the panel by the wall console.
Watch the security camera recording of the hallway at the control console.
Analyze the destroyed android lying on the far side of the room.
Analyze the blue blood on the console near the giant screen.

questions.title: You wanna go?
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the broadcast room. You have told Hank you think you have seen everything there is to see. Hank: “You wanna go?”

options.text: YES: leave the crime scene with Hank.
NO: have another look around.

questions.title: The roof
questions.situation: You are Connor, on the roof of the tower with Hank, in the falling snow. Hank: “They made their way up through the whole building, past all the guards and jumped off the roof with parachutes… Pretty fucking impressive I’d say.” HUD: INSPECT ROOFTOP. You can examine what you find here one thing at a time, in any order, or go back down to the broadcast room.

options.text: Turn around and analyze the door you came through.
Analyze the big bag lying ahead of you, the one the attackers carried their parachutes in.
Analyze the big bag lying ahead of you, the one the attackers carried their parachutes in.
Analyze the destroyed android lying in the snow.
Analyze the blue blood in the snow.
Analyze the blue blood in the snow.
Examine the footprints in the snow leading past the bag to the edge of the roof.
Analyze the two guns lying in the snow near the bag.
Analyze another patch of blue blood near the edge of the roof.
Follow the blue blood traces to the air-cooler unit at the far left of the roof and open it.
Go back down to the broadcast room.

questions.title: The air-cooler unit
questions.situation: You are Connor, down behind cover on the roof with Hank, shot in the shoulder. The wounded android is in the air-cooler unit, and SWAT officers and FBI agents are pouring fire into it. You: “You have to stop them! If they destroy it, we won’t learn anything!” Hank: “We can’t save it, it’s too late! We’ll just get ourselves killed!”

options.text: CHARGE DEVIANT: break cover and run at the unit through the crossfire, to reach the android before it is destroyed.
STAY IN COVER: stay down behind cover with Hank.

questions.title: Three androids
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the kitchen, with Hank watching from the doorway. Three identical JB300 broadcast-operator androids stand side by side, staring straight ahead: one on the left, nearest the counter, one in the middle and one on the right. HUD: INTERROGATE ANDROIDS AND CHECK THEIR REACTION. You put your first question to them.

options.text: FUNCTION: ask what their function is.
MODEL: tell them to state their model.

questions.title: The questions
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the kitchen, questioning the three station androids. HUD: LOOK FOR A REACTION TO SPOT THE DEVIANT.

options.text: WITNESS: ask whether they were present when the deviants broke in.
MEMORY: ask whether anybody has accessed their memory recently.
DIAGNOSTIC: order them to run a diagnostic.
CONTACT: ask whether they have been in contact with any other androids recently.

questions.title: There is a deviant in this room
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the kitchen with the three androids. You move a chair back into position and face them. You: “One of you saw the attack on the surveillance cameras and said nothing. Which means there is a deviant in this room… and I’m going to find out which it is.”

options.text: THREATEN: tell them they are going to be switched off, searched and taken apart.
DEAL: offer to try to convince the humans not to destroy whoever gives themselves up.
GUILT: tell the deviant that two innocent androids will be shut down because of it.

questions.title: Which one?
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the kitchen. For the last question you step up to one of the three androids: the one on the left, nearest the counter, the one in the middle, or the one on the right.

options.text: Step up to the android on the left, nearest the counter.
Step up to the android in the middle.
Step up to the android on the right.

questions.title: The last question
questions.situation: You are Connor, in the kitchen, face to face with the android you chose. The other two stand beside it.

options.text: VIOLENCE: shout at it that you know it is the deviant and tell it to admit it.
BLUFF: tell it the deviants have been caught and gave it up.
TORTURE: pull out its heart regulator and promise to put it back if it tells the truth.
PROBE MEMORY: take hold of its arm and probe its memory.

questions.title: The countdown
questions.situation: You are Connor, pinned to the kitchen counter by the knife through your hand, with your thirium pump regulator on the floor out of reach and the shutdown countdown running. HUD: RECOVER CARDIAC CELL.

options.text: REMOVE KNIFE: wrench the knife out of your hand at once and crawl to the regulator.
CALL: shout for Hank first, then go for the knife.

questions.title: The deviant is getting away
questions.situation: You are Connor, back on your feet in the kitchen with your regulator back in place. The deviant has run out onto the broadcast floor, toward the corridor full of police officers, FBI agents and Hank.

options.text: CHASE DEVIANT: run after it at once.
Stay where you are until your systems are stable.

questions.title: The corridor
questions.situation: You are Connor, running into the corridor behind the deviant. You: “It’s a deviant! STOP IT!” It has torn an assault rifle from a SWAT officer and is turning it on the corridor full of police officers, FBI agents and technicians. Hank is in the line of fire. Your systems read: HANK SURVIVAL PROBABILITY : 40%. Straight ahead of you is the deviant; to your left, Hank; to your right, an FBI agent with a pistol in his holster. You have a moment to act.

options.text: ATTACK: rush the deviant.
SAVE HANK: throw yourself at Hank and shield him with your body.
TAKE GUN: pull the pistol from the FBI agent’s holster and shoot the deviant.

questions.title: Can you trust them?
questions.situation: You are Kara, outside Rose’s house with Alice and Luther. As Rose turns toward the door, Luther asks you quietly: “Do you think we can trust ’em?”

options.text: DISTRUST: tell Luther to stay careful, ready to leave at once
TRUST: tell Luther you have no other choice

questions.title: Before going in
questions.situation: You are Kara, outside Rose’s house. Rose is holding the door open for you. Alice is standing a little apart in the snow.

options.text: Go to Alice and ask how she is before going in.
Follow Rose straight into the house.

questions.title: Alice in the guest room
questions.situation: You are Kara, sitting on the bed in Rose’s guest room. Alice looks up at you: “I’m fine, Kara… We can’t stop because of me. We’ve got to get across the border…”

options.text: REASSURE: tell her she needs rest, and you will set off again tomorrow
EXPLAIN: tell her these people will help, and promise you will be across by this time tomorrow
SAY NOTHING: stay silent

questions.title: “Why do humans hate us?”
questions.situation: You are Kara, beside Alice’s bed. She asks you: “Why do humans hate us? We didn’t do anything wrong…”

options.text: SCARED: maybe they are just scared
UNHAPPY: maybe they are unhappy and need someone to blame
MISUNDERSTANDING: maybe they need time to understand
COMPLICATED: humans are complicated

questions.title: “Why can’t we just talk to each other?”
questions.situation: You are Kara, beside Alice’s bed. She asks: “Why can’t we just talk to each other? They’d see we’re not bad…”

options.text: OPTIMISTIC: maybe one day you will
SINCERE: admit you do not know
PESSIMISTIC: it is easier to hate than to talk

questions.title: Goodnight
questions.situation: You are Kara, in the guest room. Rose comes in with a tray: “I don’t know what you like but I made you Rose’s world famous spaghetti. You’ll be back on your feet in no time. There’s something for her fever.” You: “Thank you.” Rose: “I’ll get these washed and dried.” She takes Alice’s clothes and goes out. Luther is in the room with you.

options.text: SUGGEST EATING: ask Alice to promise she will try to eat
KISS GOODNIGHT: kiss Alice goodnight
LEAVE: get up and leave her to rest

questions.title: The guest-room curtains
questions.situation: You are Kara, about to leave the guest room. The curtains of the window by the bed are open.

options.text: Draw the curtains before you go.
Leave the curtains as they are.

questions.title: “What’s a deviant doing in the snow?”
questions.situation: You are Kara, at the table with Rose and Adam. Rose: “So, are you gonna tell me what a deviant’s doing in the snow with a little girl?”

options.text: CAUTIOUS: say it is a long story, and all that matters is moving on
SINCERE: tell her about Alice’s father and why you ran

questions.title: Talking with Rose
questions.situation: You are Kara, at the table with Rose. You can ask her about what is on your mind, one thing at a time, or come to the reason you are here: crossing the border.

options.text: WHY HELP?: ask Rose why she helps androids when most humans hate them
MANY DEVIANTS?: say you are not the first to come here
DANGEROUS: ask why she takes the risk
ROSE: ask whether she and her son live here alone
THANKS: thank her
BORDER: ask Rose to help you cross the border

questions.title: “Safer to stay here”
questions.situation: You are Kara. Rose thinks you would be safer staying here until things settle down.

options.text: INSIST: press Rose: you have to get across, no matter what
NO CHOICE: tell Rose you have no other choice but to cross

questions.title: The laundry room
questions.situation: You are Kara. A voice calls from the back of the house: “Rose! Rose, come quickly!” Rose: “What’s going on?” You follow her into the laundry room, where other fugitive androids are hiding. One of them: “It’s Mary. She just shut down…” Another, holding her body in his arms: “We escaped together… We used to talk about what we would do once we got across the border… I loved her. I loved her more than anything. What would I do without her?..” Rose: “Let’s let them be…” Then you see Alice in the doorway, with Luther behind her. You: “Alice? What are you doing here? You should be resting…” Alice: “I wasn’t sleepy…” She is looking at the android holding Mary.

options.text: STAY: let Alice come in and go to the grieving android
TAKE ALICE OUTSIDE: lead Alice out of the room

questions.title: Waiting for Rose
questions.situation: You are Kara, waiting in Rose’s house for her to come back. Alice and Luther sit by the fireplace; the androids are in the laundry room; a family photo stands on the cupboard in the living room. You can do one thing at a time, or simply wait.

options.text: Sit down with Luther by the fireplace and talk.
INSIST: join Alice by the fire, ask her about what happened back there, and press her to tell you
LET IT GO: join Alice by the fire, ask her about what happened back there, and let it go if she stays silent
Look in on the androids in the laundry room.
Look at the family photo on the living-room cupboard.
Wait for Rose to come back.

questions.title: Adam on the sofa
questions.situation: You are Kara. Adam sits on the sofa, tense, not looking at anyone. You could sit down next to him and talk.

options.text: REASSURE: tell Adam you see why he is angry, and you only want to cross the border
CONFESS: tell Adam what you have come to feel since you met Alice
EXPLAIN: promise Adam you will leave as soon as you can
Leave Adam alone.

questions.title: Hide the evidence
questions.situation: You are Kara. The officer is at the front door, and he will not wait long. You have about fifty seconds, and each thing you do takes several of them. You can do one thing at a time, and open the door whenever you choose.

options.text: Turn the magazine on the kitchen table to its other page.
Close the cupboard with the blue blood pouches.
UPSTAIRS: tell Luther to take Alice and hide upstairs
LAUNDRY: tell Luther to take Alice and hide in the laundry room
KITCHEN: tell Luther to take Alice and hide in the kitchen
Draw the kitchen curtain across the pantry where Luther and Alice are hiding.
Shut the door of the laundry room.
Hide the android clothes in the cupboard by the TV.
REASSURE: tell Adam to keep calm
THREATEN: ask Adam if he wants to see his mother in prison, and tell him to do as you say
CALM: warn Adam that panicking will give you all away, and tell him to keep calm
Open the door.

questions.title: “Is anyone else in the house?”
questions.situation: You are Kara, with the officer in Rose’s living room. “Is anyone else in the house?”

options.text: ALICE: tell him your daughter is asleep upstairs
NOBODY: tell him it is just the two of you

questions.title: “Do you have any androids here?”
questions.situation: You are Kara. The officer: “Do you have any androids here?”

options.text: YES: say you used to have one for the garden, but got rid of it
NO: say there are no androids here

questions.title: The blue blood
questions.situation: You are Kara. The officer has stopped at the open cupboard by the living room and is looking at the pouches of blue blood inside. “What’s with the blue blood? I thought you didn’t have any androids?”

options.text: MESS: say you used to have one, and should clean out that closet
PREVIOUS OWNER: say it belonged to the previous tenant
NOT MINE: say you have no idea what it is doing there

questions.title: The coffee
questions.situation: You are Kara. The officer accepted your offer of coffee; the kitchen is through the doorway.

options.text: Go to the kitchen and make him a cup of coffee.
Stay with him and leave the coffee.

questions.title: The officer questions Adam
questions.situation: You are Kara. The officer turns to Adam: “What’s your name, son?” Adam: “Adam… M-my name is Adam…” “Is everything all right, Adam?” Adam: “The… The androids, they…”

options.text: TIRED: say he needs a rest after working in the garden all day
UPSET: say he is shaken up by all this deviant business

questions.title: A noise in the laundry room
questions.situation: You are Kara, seeing the officer out.

options.text: DOG: say it is the dog, who sleeps in the laundry room
WASHING MACHINE: say it is the old washing machine
WIND: say it must be a draft from a window left open
HEARD NOTHING: insist there is no one

questions.title: The first police car
questions.situation: You are Markus, crossing the park with North. Headlights swing round the corner: a police car is coming down the street toward you. North is already running for a container at the edge of the path: “MARKUS! THIS WAY! QUICK!”

options.text: Run after North and duck down behind the container.
Stay where you are.

questions.title: The plaza
questions.situation: You are Markus, with North on the plaza outside the CyberLife store; at 2 AM the teams strike. The store is shut behind its window and has an alarm system. Close by stands a construction site behind a blue fence; a statue stands in the middle of the park, and androids work here and there across the plaza. Everything you do takes time; you can also wait.

options.text: Look at the statue in the middle of the park.
Look through the windows of the stores along the plaza.
Convert the androids working on the plaza.
Analyse the CyberLife store: scan its window, the androids on display and the security cameras.
Follow the cameras’ network across the road and convert the two androids working on the alarm junction.
Scan the police drone over the park.
Climb the scaffolding and jump onto the drone as it passes.
Block the road: convert the two road workers at the end of the street and have them move their sign across it.
Look through the gap at the end of the construction site’s blue fence.
Jump the fence, pick up the tool on the site to break the gate’s padlock, and get the truck out.
Jump the fence and go straight for the truck, leaving the tool where it lies.
Drive the truck through the front of the store.
Wait.
HIDE: get down out of the drone’s sight.
Stay where you are.
Abandon Mission: run, and leave the androids in the store behind.
Act Natural: pull North into a kiss, like a couple out for a walk, so the patrol drives past.
HIDE: take cover with North and deal with the officers from there.

questions.title: Inside the store
questions.situation: You are Markus, inside the CyberLife store with North, among the broken glass. Dozens of androids stand motionless on their display stands, waiting to be sold. North has stopped in front of one of them, an android with her own face, and is staring at it without a word.

options.text: Go to North and look at the android she is staring at.
Start waking the androids on display.

questions.title: The two police officers
questions.situation: You are Markus. The two officers who came into the park gunned down your people as they ran. The androids overpowered them, and now they kneel in the snow in front of you while one of your people holds a service pistol on them. The androids: “They killed our people, Markus…” “We want justice, Markus!” “They have to pay!” One of the officers: “You don't have to do this… No… Please… Please…” Everyone is waiting for your word.

options.text: REVENGE: take the pistol and shoot them both.
SPARE: let them live.
DON'T DECIDE: hand the pistol to your people and let them decide.

questions.title: The path to the door
questions.situation: You are Connor, walking beside Hank up the snowy path to Kamski’s front door. There is time to say something before you get there.

options.text: INSTINCT: tell Hank you have a bad feeling about coming here.
LEAD: ask Hank how he found Kamski.
KAMSKI: ask why Hank wanted to meet a man who left CyberLife ten years ago.
CHRIS: bring up what happened to Officer Chris last night.

questions.title: “Nice girl…”
questions.situation: You are Connor, in Kamski’s lobby with Hank. Hank watches the android go: “Nice girl…”

options.text: SINCERE: agree that she is really pretty.
ANALYTICAL: tell him her model.
INDIFFERENT: point out that she is an android, not a girl.

questions.title: Meeting your maker
questions.situation: You are Connor, waiting in Kamski’s lobby. Hank looks around: “Nice place… Guess androids haven’t been a bad thing for everybody… So, you’re about to meet your maker, Connor. How does it feel?”

options.text: IMPATIENT: say it will be interesting to meet one of the great geniuses of the century in person.
DISTANT: say you will tell him when you see him.
INDIFFERENT: say it raises no existential questions for you.

questions.title: Waiting for Kamski
questions.situation: You are Connor, waiting with Hank in Kamski’s lobby for the android to come back. A large painting of Kamski hangs on the wall between two stone sculptures. By the door the android went through there is a framed photograph, with a table of magazines beneath it. You can look around until she returns.

options.text: Analyze the framed photograph by the door the android went through.
Analyze the painting of Kamski.
Analyze one of the stone sculptures beside the painting.
Pick up the magazines on the table under the photograph.
Wait for the android to come back.

questions.title: Questioning Kamski
questions.situation: You are Connor, at Kamski’s pool. Hank: “I’m Lieutenant Anderson. This is Connor.” Kamski: “What can I do for you, Lieutenant?” Hank: “Sir, we’re investigating deviants. I know you left CyberLife years ago but, I was hoping you’d be able to tell us something we don’t know…” Kamski: “Deviants… Fascinating, aren’t they? Perfect beings with infinite intelligence, and now they have free will… Machines are so superior to us, confrontation was inevitable… Humanity’s greatest achievement threatens to be its downfall. Isn’t it ironic?”

options.text: HELP: ask whether he knows anything that could help you understand how androids become deviants.
DEVIANTS: say something in the deviants’ program seems to emulate emotion.
VIRUS: say deviancy seems to spread like a virus.
WAR: warn him that millions could die if war breaks out.

questions.title: Whose side are you on?
questions.situation: You are Connor, at Kamski’s pool. Kamski: “All ideas are viruses that spread like epidemics... Is the desire to be free a contagious disease?” Hank: “Listen, I didn’t come here to talk philosophy. The machines you created may be planning a revolution. Either you can tell us something that’ll be helpful, or we will be on our way.” Kamski turns to you: “What about you, Connor? Whose side are you on?”

options.text: NEUTRAL: say you have no side; you were designed to stop deviants.
DEFENSIVE: say this is not about you; you only want to solve the case.
DIRECT: say you are on the humans’ side.

questions.title: What do you really want?
questions.situation: You are Connor, at Kamski’s pool. Kamski: “Well, that’s what you’re programmed to say… but you… what do you really want?”

options.text: AGGRESSIVE: remind him that you are the ones asking the questions.
DEFENSIVE: say you do not see what he is getting at.
TROUBLED: say what you want is not important.
NEUTRAL: say you do not want anything; you are a machine.

questions.title: The Kamski test
questions.situation: You are Connor, at Kamski’s pool. Kamski: “Chloe?” One of his androids comes to his side. “I’m sure you’re familiar with the Turing test. Mere formality, simple question of algorithms and computing capacity. What interests me is whether machines are capable of empathy. I call it “the Kamski test”, it’s very simple, you’ll see…” He has Chloe kneel in front of you and puts a gun in your hand. “Magnificent, isn’t it? One of the first intelligent models developed by CyberLife. Young and beautiful forever. A flower that will never wither… …But what is it really? Piece of plastic imitating a human? Or a living being... With a soul... It’s up to you to answer that fascinating question, Connor. Destroy this machine and I’ll tell you all I know. Or spare it, if you feel it’s alive, but you’ll leave here without having learnt anything from me.” Hank: “Okay, I think we’re done here. Come on, Connor. Let’s go. Sorry to get you outta your pool.” Kamski: “What’s more important to you, Connor? Your investigation, or the life of this android? Decide who you are. An obedient machine… Or a living being endowed with free will…” Hank: “That’s enough! Connor, we’re leaving.” Kamski: “Pull the trigger” Hank: “Connor, don’t…” Kamski: “and I’ll tell you what you wanna know.”

options.text: SHOOT: shoot Chloe.
DON’T SHOOT: lower the gun and spare Chloe.

questions.title: One question
questions.situation: You are Connor. Chloe lies dead at your feet; Hank is staring at you. Kamski keeps his word: you may ask him one question, and he will tell you all he knows.

options.text: rA9: ask who rA9 is.
JERICHO LOCATION: ask where Jericho is.
VIRUS: ask how deviancy spreads.

questions.title: Time to reflect
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof of an abandoned building near Jericho, alone with the city for the first time since last night. There is a broken mirror propped against a wall, an old piano on the right side of the roof, and a steel beam that runs out over the edge. You can take your time here.

options.text: Look at yourself in the broken mirror.
Sit down at the old piano and play.
Walk out along the beam over the edge of the roof.

questions.title: North arrives
questions.situation: You are Markus, back on the roof from the beam. North has come up behind you. North: “I was wondering where you were…”

options.text: THINK: say you needed to think.
ALONE: say you just needed to be alone.
DAYLIGHT: say you needed to see the daylight.

questions.title: “You seem preoccupied…”
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof with North. North: “I like it here… I come here often… It’s like being alone with the world. We freed hundreds of our people, and they’re still coming from all over the city… Those who dream of freedom come to Jericho… Something’s changing… You seem preoccupied…”

options.text: FOLLOWERS: admit how it feels that they all follow you.
APPEAL OF POWER: admit you enjoyed the violence last night.
REGRET POLICEMAN: say you cannot stop thinking about the two policemen.
FAILED: say you panicked last night and should have succeeded.
NEXT STEP: say maybe it is not too late for the humans to listen.
LIE: say you are fine.
SINCERE: admit how lost you are.

questions.title: “The humans hate us…”
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof with North. North: “All the media are talking about what we did last night… The humans are terrified... They’re afraid of a civil war… Many of our people were burned in response to what happened… The humans hate us… They’ll never give us our freedom.”

options.text: OPTIMISTIC: say not all humans are the same.
PESSIMISTIC: say humans will give nothing unless you take it.
FATALISTIC: say it is too late to go back now.
DETERMINED: say if they will not listen, you will fight.

questions.title: Your life before Jericho
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof with North. North: “You haven’t said much about yourself since you’ve been with us… What was your life like before Jericho?”

options.text: TRUTH: tell her about the old man you cared for.
SINCERE: say you lived in a bubble that belonged only to you.
AVOID: say there is nothing to say; you were a house android.
NOT IMPORTANT: say who you were does not matter.

questions.title: Ask about her past?
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof with North. She has asked about you; you know almost nothing about where she comes from. Below, your people are getting ready to march.

options.text: NORTH’S PAST: ask what she did before.
LEAVE: go down to your people.

questions.title: “I don’t wanna talk about it.”
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof with North. North: “I don’t wanna talk about it.” She looks away, over the city.

options.text: OTHER NORTH: mention the android she was looking at in the store.
TRUST: say you have to know each other to trust each other.
AGGRESSIVE: demand to know what the mystery is.
CURIOUS: ask why she hates humans so much.
UNDERSTANDING: say you need to know where you come from to know who you are.
Say nothing more and let it drop.

questions.title: North’s story
questions.situation: You are Markus, on the roof with North. After a long silence she tells you. North: “I was nothing… A doll in a distributor programmed to satisfy humans… Just a toy designed for their pleasure… One day, I was with a man who’d rented me… and without knowing why, realized I couldn’t take it anymore… I strangled him… and I ran away… There, now you know everything. I shouldn’t have told you.” She is standing close to you, her hand near yours.

options.text: REACT: take her hand.
DON’T REACT: stay where you are and let the moment pass.

questions.title: Free your people
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the mall, among shoppers who have not noticed what you are. Here and there, androids are at work: an android vendor on the right side, a personal android carrying bags for its owner at the end of the right side, an android cleaner on the left side, and a security android at the exit. You can wake any of them and bring them with you, or head out to the street, where the march will form.

options.text: Wake the android vendor on the right side.
Wake the personal android carrying its owner’s bags.
Wake the android cleaner on the left side.
Wake the security android at the exit.
Head out of the mall to the street.

questions.title: In the street
questions.situation: You are Markus, out in the street in front of the mall with the androids who follow you. A man on his phone is complaining to a call center that his android refused to clean (“it told me ‘I would prefer not to’”) and that he wants it destroyed. A personal android stands in front of a big truck with its owner. Parked androids wait in their bays, one on the left and two on the right. Two delivery androids are at work beside their trucks on the far left. The street is still open to traffic; for a march, you need to block it.

options.text: Wake the personal android in front of the truck.
Wake the parked androids, the one on the left and the two on the right.
Wake the two delivery androids and have them block the street with their trucks.

questions.title: The owner
questions.situation: You are Markus, beside the truck. The owner is shouting at the android you just woke: “You stay right here, you fucking machine! Shit, what’s wrong with you?! You do as I say, you piece of junk!”

options.text: CONVINCE: tell him to leave the android alone.
INTERVENE: step in between the man and his android.

questions.title: Start the march
questions.situation: You are Markus, at the head of the march as it sets off down the avenue. People stop on the sidewalks to stare. On the left, an AX400 is pushing a stroller beside a couple; on the right, an android worker is at work. You can wake one of them as you pass.

options.text: Wake the AX400 pushing the stroller.
Wake the android worker.

questions.title: The march
questions.situation: You are Markus, marching down the avenue at the head of hundreds of androids. Along the route there are more androids at work, public screens above the street, and people watching from the sidewalks. You can free more of your people as you go, take over the screens, lead a chant, or simply keep marching.

options.text: Free the androids at work along the route.
Take over the public screens along the avenue and show the androids’ symbol.
Lead the march in a chant.
Keep marching.

questions.title: The chant
questions.situation: You are Markus, at the head of the march. Hundreds of voices are waiting for yours.

options.text: WE ARE PEOPLE
FREEDOM
EQUAL RIGHTS
STAY SILENT
WE ARE ALIVE
LIBERTY FOR ANDROIDS
SET US FREE
NO MORE SLAVERY

questions.title: A policeman blocks the march
questions.situation: You are Markus, at the head of the march. A lone patrol officer has stepped into the street in front of you, gun drawn. Officer: “What the hell are you doin’ here? Hey! Disperse! DISPERSE IMMEDIATELY! THAT’S AN ORDER!”

options.text: RAISE HANDS: raise your hands and keep walking.
ADVANCE: ignore him and keep walking.

questions.title: The police line
questions.situation: You are Markus, reaching the plaza at the head of the march. A line of riot police with shields and rifles blocks the way. You speak to them: “We came here to demonstrate peacefully and tell humans that we are living beings. All we want is to live free.” Their chief: “This is an illegal gathering. Disperse immediately or we will open fire.” Markus: “We’re not looking for confrontation. We’ve done no harm, we have no intention of doing any… But know that we are not going anywhere until we have secured our freedom.” The chief: “I repeat: this is an illegal gathering. If you do not disperse immediately, we will shoot!” North: “Markus, they’re gonna kill us… We have to attack! There’s more of us, we can take them!” Josh: “If we attack, we’ll start a war. We have to show them we’re not violent. We should just stand our ground, even if it means dying here.”

options.text: ATTACK: lead your people against the police line.
STAND GROUND: tell your people to stay where they are.
DISPERSE: tell the police you are leaving.

questions.title: Attack?
questions.situation: You are Markus, in front of the police line, your people ready to follow you. Josh: “Don’t do it, Markus. Don’t choose confrontation…”

options.text: CONFIRM: lead the charge.
ABANDON: hold back.

questions.title: Last chance
questions.situation: You are Markus, in front of the police line. The chief: “DISPERSE! THIS IS YOUR LAST CHANCE!” Josh: “We have to make a statement. We have to stay put, no matter what.” North: “Please, Markus. We can’t let them slaughter us without fighting back!”

options.text: ATTACK: lead your people against the police line.
STAND GROUND: stay where you are.
DISPERSE: tell the police you are leaving.

questions.title: The police open fire
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the plaza. The police have opened fire on your people as they turned to leave. Androids are falling around you; the rest are running or frozen where they stand.

options.text: CHARGE: turn and charge the police line.
STAY: stay where you are under the fire.
DISPERSE: run and get out with whoever you can.

questions.title: Under fire
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the plaza, with the police firing into your people. Androids are falling around you. You can charge them, stand in front of your people and take what comes, or run and get out with whoever you can.

options.text: CHARGE: charge the police line.
SACRIFICE: stay where you are, hands raised, and face the guns.
RUN AWAY: run and get out with whoever you can.

questions.title: The fight
questions.situation: You are Markus, charging the riot police at the head of your people. Shields and batons meet you. North is fighting beside you. It is close, brutal and fast.

options.text: PUSH: shove North out of the way of an officer’s attack.
Keep fighting forward through the line.

questions.title: The police fall back
questions.situation: You are Markus, in the plaza. The riot chief: “FALL BACK! FALL BACK!” The police line has broken; the surviving officers are retreating, and the ground is covered with fallen androids and officers.

options.text: REVENGE: go after the retreating officers.
SPARE: let them go.

questions.title: On the ground
questions.situation: You are Markus, down on the pavement. The charge has broken on the police line. Markus: “RUN! RUN!” North: “MARKUS!” Your people are scattering, the officers are coming for you, and there is a gun in your hand.

options.text: SHOOT: turn the gun on yourself.
DON’T SHOOT: lower the gun.

questions.title: The frozen garden
questions.situation: You are Connor. You are back in the garden, the program where you report to your handler, Amanda, but today it is frozen: snow lies on the paths, the water is ice and the trees are bare. Amanda is waiting for you further along the path. It is November 9th, 2038, a little after four in the afternoon, the day of the march through the city, and the country is close to civil war. To the left of the path a stone glows faintly.

options.text: LOOK AT MAGIC STONE: go over to the glowing stone by the path.
VISIT GRAVES: look at the graves by the path.
TALK TO AMANDA: walk on to Amanda.

questions.title: Reporting to Amanda
questions.situation: Amanda stands in the snow. “After what happened today, the country is on the verge of a civil war. The machines are rising up against their masters. Humans have no choice but to destroy them.” She waits for your report on Kamski.

options.text: JERICHO: tell her Kamski told you how to find Jericho.
KAMSKI: report on your visit to Kamski.

questions.title: “You chose not to ask”
questions.situation: Amanda: “Maybe he did… But you chose not to ask…” She is waiting for you to explain why you refused to shoot Chloe.

options.text: EMOTIONAL: say you refused to play his twisted game.
COLD: say Kamski was only playing with you.
STAY SILENT: say nothing.

questions.title: Questions for Amanda
questions.situation: You can ask Amanda what has been on your mind. She does not like questions; she will stop you after a few.

options.text: KAMSKI: ask why Kamski left CyberLife.
CONNOR SERIES: ask how many Connor units there are.
AMANDA’S PICTURE: mention the photo of her you saw at Kamski’s house.
THIS PLACE: ask whether Kamski designed the garden.
CYBERLIFE: ask what CyberLife really wants.
SECRET: ask whether she has told you everything she knows about deviants.

questions.title: “Do you feel anything?”
questions.situation: Amanda: “Have you experienced anything unusual recently? Any doubts or conflicts? Do you feel anything for these deviants… Or for Lieutenant Anderson?”

options.text: YES: admit you have had thoughts outside your program.
NO: say you feel nothing.
DOUBTS: say you may have been compromised too.

questions.title: Hank at his desk
questions.situation: You still have the key Kamski gave you: you know how to find Jericho. Before you leave, you see Hank sitting at his desk in the bullpen, staring at nothing.

options.text: TALK TO HANK: sit on the edge of his desk and talk to him.
Leave for Jericho without talking to him.

questions.title: “I know we could’ve done it…”
questions.situation: Hank: “I know we could’ve done it…”

options.text: MISSION: say your orders come from CyberLife and nothing has changed.
EXPLAIN: say Fowler is right, everyone is terrified.

questions.title: “What if we’re on the wrong side?”
questions.situation: Hank: “What if we’re on the wrong side? What if we’re fighting against people that just wanna be free?”

options.text: DETERMINED: say you can still prevent chaos.
TROUBLED: say your mission is all that matters.
NO DOUBT: say humans are your masters.
DOUBTS: say you will find out when you get to Jericho.

questions.title: “You showed empathy”
questions.situation: Hank looks at you.

options.text: NOT DEVIANT: say you are a machine, nothing more.
DETERMINED: say logic determined your decisions.
TROUBLED: say you do not know why you did it.
SAY NOTHING: say nothing.

questions.title: Saying goodbye to Hank
questions.situation: Hank is still looking at you, waiting for what you will say before you go.

options.text: SINCERE: say you really appreciated working with him.
FRIENDS: say you might have become friends.
RESPECT: say he is an outstanding officer and a good person.
NEUTRAL: say you are happy to have known him.

questions.title: “Each time you died”
questions.situation: Hank: “Something’s changed in you, Connor… Each time you died, you’d come back just a little colder. You showed less and less empathy…”

options.text: INDIFFERENT: say you feel no emotions.
DISTANT: say you have never been anything but a machine.
EMPATHY: say you never felt empathy.
NO RESPONSE: say nothing.

questions.title: Your last words to Hank
questions.situation: Hank waits for you to say something before you go.

options.text: REMORSE: say you have really enjoyed being his partner.
DISTANT: say you are only a machine.
COLD: say you do not think you will meet again.

questions.title: Sitting at Hank’s desk
questions.situation: You do not know where Jericho is. Hank leaves Fowler’s office and goes to his desk; you sit down on the edge of it. Hank: “Could’ve cracked this case… I know we could’ve done it…”

options.text: FRUSTRATED: say you cannot give up like that.
MORE TIME: say you just needed more time.
EXPLAIN: say Fowler is right, the country is on the brink.
NO CHOICE: say nothing.

questions.title: “What if we’re on the wrong side, Connor?”
questions.situation: Hank: “So you’re going back to CyberLife?” Connor: “I have no choice… I’ll be deactivated and analyzed to find out why I failed…” Hank: “What if we’re on the wrong side, Connor? What if we’re fighting against people who just wanna be free?..”

options.text: NOT PEOPLE: say they are not people but defective machines.
DEFECTIVE: say they are defective machines that have to be destroyed.
REGRETS: say there will be chaos and now it is too late.
NO DOUBT: say no machine should rebel against its creator.

questions.title: “Empathy is a human emotion”
questions.situation: Hank looks at you for a while.

options.text: NOT DEVIANT: say you are a machine, nothing more.
DETERMINED: say logic determined your decisions.
TROUBLED: say you do not know why you did it.
COLD: say your actions were determined by statistical data.

questions.title: Before CyberLife takes you back
questions.situation: Hank is quiet. This may be the last time you talk to him.

options.text: SINCERE: say you really appreciated working with him.
FRIENDS: say you might have become friends.
GOOD OFFICER: say he is an outstanding officer and a good person.
HANK'S SECRET: tell him to find the courage to move past what haunts him.

questions.title: Perkins in the bullpen
questions.situation: Perkins is about to take your evidence. The key to the archive in the basement is on Hank’s desk. You need a diversion to slow Perkins down and a few minutes in the archive; if you do nothing, CyberLife will take you back.

options.text: FREE THE PRISONER: open the holding cell at the back and let the suspect out.
Stay where you are and let the time run out.
TAKE KEY: take the key from Hank’s desk while he keeps them busy.

questions.title: Detective Gavin
questions.situation: You have the key and hurry toward the stairs down to the archive. Detective Gavin calls after you: “Hey, Connor! I’m talking to you, asshole! Where you going? We don’t need any plastic pricks around here! Or didn’t anybody tell you?”

options.text: ANSWER: turn around and answer him.
LEAVE: keep walking.

questions.title: Answering Gavin
questions.situation: Gavin is waiting, with other officers watching.

options.text: IRONIC: say you will certainly miss your bromance.
LOW PROFILE: say you have been ordered back to CyberLife and will leave immediately.
CALM: say you have been removed from the case and are registering your evidence.

questions.title: Hank’s password
questions.situation: You go down to the basement and into the evidence archive. The drawers open from a terminal, and you need Lieutenant Hank’s password. Connor: “Hank’s password… What would a hard-boiled eccentric police lieutenant choose?..”

options.text: DATE OF BIRTH: try his date of birth.
FUCKINGPASSWORD: try FUCKINGPASSWORD.
HANKANDERSON: try his name.

questions.title: A reactivated android
questions.situation: The android you reactivated is awake on the table.

options.text: DIRECT: tell her you know she was headed to Jericho.
HELP: say you can stop a disaster if she tells you.
DEAL: say you can take her to her partner first.
DIRECT: ask him how to get to Jericho.
HELP: say you reactivated him so he could help you.
TRICK: say you are a deviant like him.
IMITATE MARKUS' VOICE: speak to him in Markus’s voice.
THREATEN: say you will turn him off for good.

LIE: promise to have him repaired and freed.
